prompt:
Trino temporal types and literals lose their fractional-second precision. In Trino, CAST(... AS TIMESTAMP(n)) and TIME(n), with or without WITH TIME ZONE, should keep the precision, and TIMESTAMP/TIME '...' literals should become casts whose precision matches the literal's fractional digits. Presto only supports millisecond precision, so generating Presto from any other precision should drop it and warn "Presto only supports millisecond precision for temporal types" (raising under ErrorLevel.RAISE).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("SELECT TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01 00:00:00.10'", read="trino").sql("trino")
# currently: SELECT CAST('2020-01-01 00:00:00.10' AS TIMESTAMP)
# expected:  SELECT CAST('2020-01-01 00:00:00.10' AS TIMESTAMP(2))

parse_one("CAST('2020-01-01 00:00:00.123' AS TIMESTAMP(6))", read="trino").sql("presto")
# currently: CAST('2020-01-01 00:00:00.123' AS TIMESTAMP(6))
# expected:  CAST('2020-01-01 00:00:00.123' AS TIMESTAMP)

parse_one("SELECT TIME '12:00:00.1'", read="trino").sql("trino")
# currently: SELECT CAST('12:00:00.1' AS TIME)
# expected:  SELECT CAST('12:00:00.1' AS TIME(1))
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.

 class TestPresto(Validator):
     dialect = "presto"
 
+    def test_temporal_precision(self):
+        message = "Presto only supports millisecond precision for temporal types"
+        for kind, value in (("TIMESTAMP", "2020-01-01 00:00:00"), ("TIME", "12:00:00")):
+            for zone in ("", " +02:00"):
+                suffix = " WITH TIME ZONE" if zone else ""
+                expected = f"CAST('{value}.123{zone}' AS {kind}{suffix})"

+                        if precision in ("", "(3)"):
+                            self.assertEqual(
+                                expression.sql("presto", unsupported_level=ErrorLevel.RAISE),
+                                expected,
+                            )
+                        else:
+                            with self.assertLogs(generator_logger) as logs:
+                                self.assertEqual(expression.sql("presto"), expected)
+                            self.assertIn(message, logs.output[0])
+                            with self.assertRaisesRegex(UnsupportedError, message):
+                                expression.sql("presto", unsupported_level=ErrorLevel.RAISE)
